subject: Cloud Computing
title: PaaS: Just Deploy Your Code
description: Learn PaaS: Just Deploy Your Code in one minute.

hook.text: What if you could push code and it just runs — no servers to configure, no OS to patch?

buildup.text: PaaS handles the infrastructure. You provide the application code, and the platform does the rest.

discovery.text: Heroku popularized PaaS in 2007. Push your code with git and your app is live in seconds.

twist.text: PaaS is magical until you need something custom. Then the platform's constraints become your cage.

climax.text: PaaS is perfect for teams that want to build fast without infrastructure expertise.

punchline.text: PaaS hides the servers. You just ship the code.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of PaaS over IaaS?
options: Developers deploy code without managing servers or operating systems
PaaS is always cheaper than IaaS
PaaS provides physical hardware for customers to customize

details.summary: PaaS handles the operating system, runtime, middleware, and scaling so developers can focus entirely on writing and deploying code. Services like AWS Elastic Beanstalk, Azure App Service, and Google App Engine abstract away infrastructure management completely.
details.whyItMatters: PaaS dramatically accelerates development by eliminating infrastructure work. Teams ship features faster when they do not need to manage servers, patches, or scaling logic.
takeaways: PaaS manages infrastructure so developers focus on code
Auto-scaling and patching are handled by the platform
Deployment is as simple as pushing code or a container

faq.question: What is the main advantage of PaaS over IaaS?
faq.answer: PaaS eliminates OS patching, runtime updates, and capacity planning. Developers deploy code and the platform handles scaling, load balancing, and health monitoring. This reduces operational overhead dramatically, especially for smaller teams.

faq.question: What languages do PaaS platforms typically support?
faq.answer: Most PaaS platforms support popular languages including Node.js, Python, Java, .NET, Ruby, PHP, and Go. Many also support Docker containers, allowing any language or framework that can be containerized to run on the platform.
